claim: Complete list of PowerToys utilities shipping as of 2026, used to break PowerToys down per module.
quote: The currently available utilities include: Advanced Paste, Always On Top, Awake, Color Picker, Command Not Found, Command Palette, Crop And Lock, Environment Variables, FancyZones, File Explorer add-ons, File Locksmith, Grab And Move, Hosts File Editor, Image Resizer, Keyboard Manager, Light Switch, Mouse utilities, Mouse Without Borders, New+, Peek, Power Display, PowerRename, PowerToys Run, Quick Accent, Registry Preview, Screen Ruler, Shortcut Guide, Text Extractor, Workspaces, ZoomIt

claim: Community consensus in 2026 is that no single Linux tool replaces AutoHotkey; users must combine several, and window automation is DE/WM-specific.
quote: Afaik you won't find a single alternative, but you'll have to find multiple projects for specific features... Window automation is DE/WM specific.

claim: keyd remaps at the evdev/uinput kernel layer and is therefore display-server agnostic, working under X11, Wayland and bare VTs.
quote: kernel level input primitives (evdev, uinput)

claim: kanata's documented Linux limitations: unicode output depends on ibus, and rapid key events can misfire.
quote: Unicode support has varying success due to many applications not supporting the `ibus` input mechanism. Using xkb to map keys to unicode or using clipboard actions are more consistent solutions

claim: keymapper is the closest structural analogue to AutoHotkey's per-application context rules, but on Wayland the compositor must feed it focus information via a GNOME Shell extension or KWin script, and process paths may be unavailable.
quote: To make context awareness work under Wayland, the compositor has to inform `keymapper`

claim: Espanso ships separate X11 and Wayland builds; Wayland support is experimental, needs setcap, and has documented limitations around keyboard layouts, app-specific config and hotplugged keyboards.
quote: Wayland support is currently experimental, therefore some features might be missing or not working well yet.

claim: Upstream AutoKey is an Xorg application and does not function in a Wayland session.
quote: AutoKey is a Xorg application and will not function in a Wayland session.

claim: The autokey-wayland fork is the only AutoKey that runs under Wayland, and only on GNOME (KDE support planned).
quote: This version of AutoKey currently only works with Gnome desktops under Wayland. Under X11, it continues to work with any desktop environment.

claim: ydotool synthesises input through the kernel uinput framework instead of X events, so it works on Wayland, but its daemon needs access to /dev/uinput which normally means root.
quote: xdotool sends X events directly to X server, while ydotool uses the uinput framework of Linux kernel to emulate an input device.

claim: libei is integrated into the XDG RemoteDesktop and InputCapture portals since portal 1.17, with session persistence since 1.21, giving compositor-independent input emulation.
quote: libei is now a part of the XDG Remote Desktop portal and the XDG Input Capture (both since version 1.17, mid 2023)

claim: GlobalShortcuts portal coverage is uneven in 2026: wlroots-based compositors ship no implementation at all, so BindShortcuts fails.
quote: wlroots' `xdg-desktop-portal-wlr` ships no GlobalShortcuts implementation, so on Niri `BindShortcuts` fails with `error code 5`.

claim: GNOME 50 (March 2026) removed the X11 session entirely; X11 apps only run via XWayland.
quote: GNOME 50 is Wayland-only, and X11 support has been completely removed. However, X11 app support is still there; there is just no longer an X11 session.

claim: KDE Plasma 6.8, due October 2026, drops the X11 session and goes Wayland-only.
quote: From Plasma 6.8 in October 2026, only Wayland will be available at login

claim: Flameshot's own docs document Wayland breakage — repeated portal permission prompts on GNOME, multi-monitor overlay problems, and shortcuts that fail to trigger.
quote: We cannot do anything about it!

claim: CopyQ works on Wayland with caveats: global shortcuts need xdg-desktop-portal, native clipboard monitoring works on KDE/Sway/wlroots, GNOME needs a Shell extension, and modifier/mouse-position queries do not work.
quote: Querying keyboard modifier state and mouse position does not work on Wayland.

claim: Comparison of Linux disk-usage analysers (QDirStat, K4DirStat, Baobab, Filelight, ncdu) establishing QDirStat as the closest WinDirStat analogue.
quote: Linux Disk Usage Tools Compared: QDirStat vs. K4DirStat vs. Baobab vs. Filelight vs. ncdu

claim: 7-Zip ships an official Linux console build (version 26.02, 2026-06-25) for x86-64, x86, arm64 and arm.
quote: 7-Zip for Linux: console version

claim: Power Automate for desktop installs only via a Windows MSI or the Microsoft Store and depends on the Windows Desktop .NET runtime — there is no Linux build.
quote: Download and install Power Automate using an MSI installer or from Microsoft Store.

claim: pdftk-java is a maintained Java port of PDFtk that keeps the same command-line interface on Linux.
quote: pdftk-java emerged as a port to Java, maintaining compatibility while enabling continued development

claim: 1Password for Linux ships deb, rpm, SUSE repo, AUR, tar.gz, Flatpak and Snap packages; the Flatpak build loses system authentication, the SSH agent, and unified app/browser unlock.
quote: You won't be able to use the SSH agent.

claim: 1Password on Linux can be unlocked with the Linux user password, fingerprint or other biometrics, or a security key.
quote: your Linux user password, instead of your 1Password account password

claim: Notepad++ has no official Linux build; the Wine/Snap route is an unofficial third-party effort the Notepad++ team is not involved in.
quote: it is not supported on Linux, so there really isn't any such thing as the "Notepad++ approach." The technique used to get Notepad++ running on Linux is an unofficial effort, and the Notepad++ development team have nothing to do with it.

claim: RustDesk captures the screen on Wayland via PipeWire and the XDG desktop portal with a remembered consent dialog, supports multi-monitor since 1.4.3, and supports a permanent password for unattended access.
quote: On Wayland it captures the screen through PipeWire and the XDG desktop portal, which shows a consent dialog to pick a display

claim: KDE Connect exceeds Phone Link on features — bidirectional clipboard, remote input, command execution, file sharing — over LAN with no cloud account.
quote: KDE Connect works over your existing Wi-Fi network (no cloud, no Microsoft account, no Bluetooth drama).

claim: On Linux, Firejail is the lowest-friction Sandboxie analogue for distro-packaged apps; bubblewrap is the low-level primitive with no ready-made profiles; Flatpak only confines Flatpak-installed apps.
quote: Flatpak uses Bubblewrap under the hood and adds a portals-based permission system, but it only confines applications that you install through Flatpak.

claim: The crowd-ranked Linux replacements for IrfanView are XnView MP (closest, closed-source), then nomacs, gThumb, qView, Gwenview and qimgv.
quote: The best Linux alternative is XnView MP.

claim: Pinta is the crowd-ranked closest free/open replacement for Paint.NET on Linux, with Krita and GIMP as heavier alternatives.
quote: The best Linux alternative is Pinta, which is both free and Open Source.

claim: Per-module PowerToys mappings on Linux: Albert for PowerToys Run, NormCap for Text Extractor, Gpick/KColorChooser/Pick for Color Picker, a file renamer for PowerRename.
quote: For extracting text, install NormCap from the Software Manager. NormCap works much like Text Extractor.

claim: Kdenlive, Shotcut and OpenShot are the free/open Linux replacements for Clipchamp.
quote: Best Free and Open Source Alternatives to Microsoft Clipchamp

claim: ClamAV is a signature scanner, not an EDR: no behavioural analysis, memory scanning or automated response.
quote: ClamAV has no behavioral analysis, memory scanning, or automated response capability

claim: UI.Vision RPA is a cross-platform (Linux included) open-source RPA tool positioned as a desktop/web automation replacement, running locally.
quote: Free, Open-Source RPA Software 2025 for macOS, Linux and Windows

claim: Sandboxie-Plus is a Windows-only sandbox built on Windows kernel drivers; there is no Linux port.
quote: Sandboxie - Sandbox software for application isolation and secure web browsing
